answers.question: Can I do all three runs next week and add the two I missed?
answers.answer:
No. Missed runs are best left missed. Adding them would squeeze five sessions into one week while you're still getting over a fever.

Next week has two slightly shorter walk-runs, on Wednesday and Saturday. Monday stays a rest day while you finish recovering. Run on Wednesday only if the fever has stayed away, the cough is easing and you no longer feel wiped out.

If Wednesday goes well, Saturday is a little longer. The week after can go back to your full 24-minute session.

new.analysis:
## How the week went
You did Monday exactly as planned: 24 minutes of 2 minutes running and 1 minute walking, at effort 6/10. Then the cold wiped out Wednesday and Saturday. That left one run and 2.78 km for the week, against about 7 km in each of the two weeks before. Not running with a fever was the right call.

## Why next week steps back
After a fever and several days of feeling wiped out, the goal is to come back without setting yourself back. The two walk-runs use the same 2-minute run, 1-minute walk pattern you already know, just with fewer repeats. Starting smaller lets you test how your body copes before going back to your full session.

## Monday's heart rate
Monday's heart rate ran higher than your earlier runs, even though it didn't feel any harder.

| Run | Avg heart rate | Time in zone 3 | Effort |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sat Aug 29 | 132 | 25% | 7/10 |
| Mon Aug 31 | 133 | 33% | 6/10 |
| Wed Sep 2 | 132 | 24% | 5/10 |
| Sat Sep 5 | 136 | 45% | 7/10 |
| Mon Sep 7 | 139 | 83% | 6/10 |

The cold showed up the next day, but one run on its own doesn't tell us much. When you're back, compare your runs with the 132 to 136 range. It's a simple way to see whether you're ready for more.

## The road to November
Running the whole 5K is still realistic in eight weeks, though it will take steady weeks from here. At your stage, building means making the running stretches longer bit by bit, not running faster. Pushing through now and getting ill again would cost far more time than one easy week.

safetyCallouts.title: Get the cough checked if it hangs on.
safetyCallouts.body: If it isn't clearly easing over the next week, gets worse, or the fever comes back, see your GP before running again.

safetyCallouts.title: Stop if you get chest symptoms.
safetyCallouts.body: If you feel chest pain, a racing or fluttering heartbeat, dizziness or unusual breathlessness while running, stop and see a doctor promptly.
